```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>",
  echo = TRUE,
  eval = TRUE,
  fig.height = 6,
  fig.width = 9,
  fig.align='center'

```

```{r setup, echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyverse)
library(summarySCI)
```


The function `boxplotSCI()` generates boxplots of a variable 
of interest (such as a quality of life score, for example) for one time point or 
over time for one or two groups. 


## Setup and data

To demonstrate the various functionalities,
we will use the dataset `summarySCI::hemoglobin_data`.

```{r, message = FALSE}
library(summarySCI)
data(hemoglobin_data)
hemoglobin <- hemoglobin_data
```





```{r, echo = FALSE}
n_patients <- length(unique(hemoglobin$ID))
n_timepoints <- length(unique(hemoglobin$visit_nr))
```

The dataset `hemoglobin` contains the hemoglobin values of `r n_patients` patients
at `r n_timepoints` different time points. 
The time points in the column `visit_nr`
are coded as numeric, while the time points in column 
`visit` are coded as factor. 
The column `Arm` indicates 
whether the patient was in `Arm A` or `Arm B`. 

```{r}
head(hemoglobin)
```


## Basic boxplots for two groups

```{r}
boxplotSCI(data = hemoglobin, 
                  var = hb, 
                  order = visit_nr, 
                  group = Arm, 
                  main = "Boxplots for the two groups", 
                  legend_position = "topleft")
```

Now let us imagine that we want the order of the treatment groups to be 
reversed.

```{r}
hemoglobin$Arm <- factor(hemoglobin$Arm, levels = c("Arm B", 
                                                "Arm A"))

boxplotSCI(data = hemoglobin, 
                  var = hb, 
                  order = visit_nr, 
                  group = Arm, 
                  main = "Reversed treatment order", 
                  legend_position = "topright")

```

## Group names

The names of the two groups can be customized using 
`group_names` (for the legend) and `group_names_short`
for the x-axis. 
The order in `group_names` and `group_names_short`
must match the order of `levels(factor(data$group))`

```{r}
# back to original order
hemoglobin$Arm <- factor(hemoglobin$Arm, levels = c("Arm A", 
                                                "Arm B"))

boxplotSCI(data = hemoglobin, 
                  var = hb, 
                  order = visit_nr, 
                  group = Arm, 
                  group_names = c("Treatment (Arm A)", "Control (Arm B)"), 
                  group_names_short = c("A", "B"),
                  main = "Customization of group names", 
                  legend_position = "topright")

```


## One group
The function can also be used when there is only one group.
```{r, fig.width = 10}
boxplotSCI(data = hemoglobin[hemoglobin$Arm == "Arm A", ], # Only treatment
                  var = hb, 
                  order = visit_nr,
                  main = "Only treatment group")
```

## Time points as factors

The function also accept time points given as factors.
In this case, the user needs to make sure that 
the factor is correctly ordered. 

```{r}
hemoglobin$visit <- factor(hemoglobin$visit,
                           levels = c("Cycle 1", "Cycle 2", "Cycle 3", 
                                      "Cycle 4", "Cycle 5", "Cycle 6", 
                                      "Cycle 7", "Cycle 8", "Cycle 9"))
```


```{r}
boxplotSCI(data = hemoglobin, 
                  var = hb, 
                  order = visit, 
                  group = Arm, 
                  group_names = c("Treatment (Arm A)", "Control (Arm B)"), 
                  group_names_short = c("A", "B"),
                  main = "Time points as factor", 
                  legend_position = "topleft"
                  )

```

Another equivalent alternative is to put the numeric time points
in `order` and the labels in `visit`. 

```{r}

boxplotSCI(data = hemoglobin, 
                  var = hb, 
                  order = visit_nr, 
                  visit = visit,
                  group = Arm, 
                  group_names = c("Treatment (Arm A)", "Control (Arm B)"), 
                  group_names_short = c("A", "B"),
                  main = "Time points as factor", 
                  legend_position = "topleft"
                  )

```


## Customization of the boxplots


### Legend 

The position and size of the legend can easily 
be adapted using the arguments `legend_position`
and `legend_cex`, respectively. 
A box can be added around the legend using `legend_bty = "o"`. 

```{r}
boxplotSCI(data = hemoglobin, 
                  var = hb, 
                  order = visit_nr, 
                  group = Arm, 
                  # short names
                  group_names = c("Treatment (Arm A)", "Control (Arm B)"), 
                  group_names_short = c("A", "B"),
                  # Title
                  main = "Hemoglobin over time", 
                  # Legend position
                  legend_position = "bottomright",
                  # Legend size
                  legend_cex = 0.75, 
                  # Legend box
                  legend_bty = "o"
                  )

```

### Size and color of boxes
The color and size of the boxes can be customized using the arguments
`col` and `boxwex`. The distance between the boxes (when two groups are compared)
can be adjusted with the argument `shift`. 


```{r}

boxplotSCI(data = hemoglobin, 
                  var = hb, 
                  order = visit_nr, 
                  group = Arm, 
                  # short names
                  group_names = c("Treatment (Arm A)", "Control (Arm B)"), 
                  group_names_short = c("A", "B"),
                  # Title
                  main = "Hemoglobin over time", 
                  # Col of boxes
                  col = c("lightblue", "orange"),
                  # Width of boxes
                  boxwex = 0.2, 
                  #Space between boxes
                  shift = 0.15,
                  # Legend position
                  legend_position = "topleft",
                  )

```


### Axes 

Various parameters related to the axes can be customized using 
`xlab`, `ylab`, `cex_lab`, `cex_axis`, `ylim` and `y_ticks`. 

```{r}
par(las = 1)
boxplotSCI(data = hemoglobin, 
                  var = hb, 
                  order = visit_nr, 
                  group = Arm, 
                  group_names = c("Treatment (Arm A)", "Control (Arm B)"), 
                  group_names_short = c("A", "B"),
                  # Title
                  main = "Hemoglobin over time", 
                  # X axis label
                  xlab = "Visits", 
                  # X axis position
                  xlab_position = 0,
                  # Y axis label
                  ylab = "Score",
                  # Size of axis labels
                  cex_lab = 1.2,
                  # Size of axes
                  cex_axis = 1.1,
                  # Size of number of patients
                  cex_n_patients = 0.9,
                  # Y axis limit
                  ylim = c(80, 200),
                  # Y axis ticks
                  y_ticks = seq(80, 180, by = 10),
                  legend_position = "topleft"
                  )

```


### Lines and colors

Lines can be added using `lines` and their color and type
specified using `col_lines` and `lty`, respectively.

```{r}

boxplotSCI(data = hemoglobin, 
                  var = hb, 
                  order = visit_nr, 
                  group = Arm, 
                  group_names = c("Treatment (Arm A)", "Control (Arm B)"), 
                  group_names_short = c("A", "B"),
                  # Title
                  main = "Hemoglobin over time", 
                  # Col of boxes
                  col = c("lightblue", "orange"),
                  # X axis label
                  xlab = "Visits", 
                  # X axis position
                  xlab_position = 0,
                  # Y axis label
                  ylab = "Score",
                  lines = c(90, 120, 160), 
                  # Col of lines
                  col_lines = c("red", "grey", "red"), 
                  # Type of lines
                  lty = c(2, 3, 2)
                  )

```


## Special case: only one time point
The function also works if no intput is provided for `order` or if `order`
only contains one time point.
```{r}
par(las = 1)
boxplotSCI(data = hemoglobin[hemoglobin$visit_nr == 4, ], 
                  var = hb, 
                  # order = visit_nr, 
                  group = Arm, 
                  main = "Only one time point"
                  )

```

## Time point is missing for one group 

The function also works if one (or more) time points are missing 
for one of the groups. 
The argument `missing_nr` controls what should 
be displayed for the number of patients for the missing time point. 
Default to `0`.
For example, let us assume that there is no 
hemoglobin value for the patient in the `Arm A` group 
at time point `8`: 
```{r}
 
hemoglobin_2 <- hemoglobin[!(hemoglobin$Arm == "Arm A" & hemoglobin$visit_nr == 8), ]


# numeric
boxplotSCI(data = hemoglobin_2,
                var = hb,
                order = visit_nr,
                group_names = c("Treatment (Arm A)", "Control (Arm B)"), 
                group_names_short = c("A", "B"),
                group = Arm,
                main = "Boxplots for the two groups", 
                legend_position = "topleft", 
                missing_nr = 0)

```

Now let us imagine that there is no hemoglobin value
for the patients in the `Arm B` group after timepoint 4:
```{r}


hemoglobin_3 <- hemoglobin[!(hemoglobin$Arm == "Arm B" & hemoglobin$visit_nr > 4), ]


# numeric
boxplotSCI(data = hemoglobin_3,
                var = hb,
                order = visit_nr,
                group_names = c("Treatment (Arm A)", "Control (Arm B)"), 
                group_names_short = c("A", "B"),
                group = Arm,
                main = "Boxplots for the two groups", 
                legend_position = "topleft", 
                missing_nr = NA)



```
